case.summary: The monitoring sweep on card C12352-K2 identified a $2,161.07 in person transaction on 2016-12-14 that received a fraud verdict at probability 0.76 under pattern account_takeover. Four of the card-detail match flags M1-M9 returned F, step-up authentication was not completed, and the amount was 36.6x the card's median and above its 95th percentile. Connected components over the device-sharing graph placed the card in a bounded component of 2 cards including C11164-K1, and the 5 closed cases CC-3361, CC-4839, CC-4470, CC-4562, and CC-5544 closed as 5 confirmed fraud and 0 cleared. Under policy rule R8, rule R4, and rule R6, the case was escalated, the card was named for monitoring, and the transaction was declined.

sar.narrative: Between 2016-12-14 and 2016-12-14, card C12352-K2 belonging to customer C12352 was used for 1 transaction(s) totalling $2,161.07, of which the transaction that triggered this investigation was $2,161.07 on 2016-12-14. The activity was conducted in person under product code W, billed in region 330.0. 4 of the card-detail match flags M1-M9 came back F on this transaction. Step-up authentication was not completed. The same device profile was used by 1 other card(s) in the thirty days to 2016-12-14 (C11164-K1), indicating a common actor operating across more than one cardholder. On contact, no reply within 24 hours. That response is an assumption recorded in the case file, as no cardholder replies were available to this investigation. The activity is suspicious because it is consistent with mixed-channel activity consistent with stolen credentials, assessed at a 76% probability of being fraudulent on 3 independent pieces of evidence drawn from the transaction graph and the institution's closed-case history. The filing is made because the loss exposure of $2,161.07 exceeds the institution's $1,000 reporting threshold. The total amount of suspicious activity is $2,161.07. The card has been placed under heightened monitoring, the pending authorisation has been declined, the matter has been escalated to a fraud analyst, an internal investigation case has been opened, and the cards sharing the same origin have been placed under monitoring.
